scientific_principle: A magnetic space group is a group of affine operations (rotation W, translation w, time-reversal label) leaving a magnetic structure invariant. Changing the coordinate setting by a Jones-Faithful transformation T(x)=P x+p conjugates every operation: g' = T g T^-1, with W' = P W P^-1, w' = P w + p - W' p, and an unchanged time-reversal label. Consequently the group order, the multiset of time-reversal labels, the rotation axes, and the orbit of any site are preserved up to the coordinate map: the orbit in the new setting is exactly T applied to the orbit in the original setting. Archive records storing the same physical magnetic symmetry under different producer conventions (different transform_BNS_Pp_abc strings) must therefore yield conjugate operation families so that downstream catalogue analysis is convention-independent.
violated_invariant: The magnetic operation family returned for a BNS number under a non-identity transform_BNS_Pp_abc setting is not the conjugate T*G*T^-1 of the standard BNS family, so the producer's setting transformation is not correctly applied and the scientific meaning (rotation axes, origin-shifted translations, orbits, time-reversal structure) is not preserved across conventions.
observable_symptom: For records whose transform_BNS_Pp_abc is not the identity, the computed operation family / probe orbit disagrees with the conjugate of the BNS-standard family: rotation axes are not carried to the producer's axes, non-half-integer origin shifts do not shift the translations, and the orbit of a site in the producer's coordinates is not T applied to the orbit in the BNS-standard coordinates.
acceptance_checks: For any BNS number N and Jones-Faithful setting T, the returned operations form the conjugate family T*G_N*T^-1: same group order, rotation parts equal to P*W*P^-1 of the standard family, identical time-reversal labels, and translations P*w+p-W'*p (mod 1).
The orbit of a probe site expressed in the producer's coordinates equals T applied to the orbit of T^-1(probe) in the BNS-standard setting.
The total operation count and the multiset of time-reversal labels are invariant under the choice of setting for a fixed BNS number.
The identity setting 'a,b,c;0,0,0' returns exactly the standard BNS operations (no spurious transformation).

The invariance holds for basis permutations, axis inversions, and non-half-integer origin shifts on BNS numbers other than the supplied record, including groups with non-central rotations (e.g. a 2-fold axis) where the rotation part must change under a basis swap.

metamorphic_probes.name: identity_setting_noop
metamorphic_probes.relation: Transform T = identity: the operation family for setting 'a,b,c;0,0,0' must equal the standard BNS family exactly (rotation, translation mod 1, time label). Guard against over-correction.

metamorphic_probes.name: origin_shift_conjugation
metamorphic_probes.relation: Transform T = pure origin shift (P=I, p non-half-integer): the returned family must equal the conjugate, which exercises w' = P w + p - W' p; a non-half-integer shift is non-trivial even for the central-rotation group P-1. Fails before fix.

metamorphic_probes.name: basis_change_rotation_conjugation
metamorphic_probes.relation: Transform T = basis swap/inversion on a low-symmetry group with a non-central rotation: the rotation parts of the returned family must equal P*W*P^-1 of the standard family (the rotation set must change), and the full family must match the conjugate. Fails before fix; catches translation-only fixes.

metamorphic_probes.name: orbit_covariance
metamorphic_probes.relation: For a non-symmetry setting T (verified to change the family), the orbit of a random probe in producer coordinates under the returned family must equal T applied to the orbit of T^-1(probe) under the standard BNS family. Fails before fix.

metamorphic_probes.name: time_label_count_invariance
metamorphic_probes.relation: Across several settings (identity, swap, inversion, origin shift) of the same BNS number (a black-white group so both time labels occur), the operation count and the multiset of time-reversal labels must be invariant. Guard against count changes or dropped time labels.

import sys
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from collections import Counter
for base in [Path.cwd(), Path.cwd().parent]:
    src = base/'source'
    if src.exists():
        sys.path.insert(0, str(src)); break
from pymatgen.io.cif import CifParser, MagneticCifBlock
from pymatgen.symmetry.maggroups import MagneticSpaceGroup
def get(N,s):
    G=CifParser().get_magsymops(MagneticCifBlock({"_space_group_magn.number_BNS":str(N),
        "_space_group_magn.transform_BNS_Pp_abc":s}))
    if isinstance(G,Exception): raise G
    return G
N=231
G=MagneticSpaceGroup(N).symmetry_ops()
ref=Counter(int(op.time_reversal) for op in G)
ok=True
for s in ["a,b,c;0,0,0","b,a,c;0,0,0","a,-b,c;0,0,0","a,b,c;0.25,0,0"]:
    H=get(N,s)
    if len(H)!=len(G) or Counter(int(op.time_reversal) for op in H)!=ref: ok=False; break
print("PASS" if ok else "FAIL")

anti_hardcoding: Returning the standard BNS operations for every setting (silently ignoring transform_BNS_Pp_abc) passes the identity and count/label guards but fails origin_shift_conjugation, basis_change_rotation_conjugation, and orbit_covariance on any non-symmetry setting.
Hardcoding the corrected family or transformation for the supplied record's BNS number / setting string fails on the other BNS numbers and settings that the adaptive probes search over.

Applying the Jones-Faithful conjugation in the wrong direction (T^-1 g T instead of T g T^-1) or with a wrong origin-shift sign passes rotation-only checks on central-rotation groups but fails the origin-shift and orbit-covariance probes.

Handling only the translation/origin part (not conjugating the rotation) passes the origin-shift probe on central-rotation groups (e.g. P-1) but fails the basis-change probe on groups with non-central rotations (e.g. P2).
Forcing the time-reversal label to +1 passes count checks on gray groups but fails the time-label invariance probe on a black-white group.
evidence_notes: The immutable workflow passes the producer convention only via MagneticCifBlock['_space_group_magn.transform_BNS_Pp_abc'] into CifParser.get_magsymops; that is the single source-side entry point that receives the setting, so the setting must be applied there (or in a helper it calls).

The maggroups.py outline shows MagneticSpaceGroup has no method to change its setting, so unless get_magsymops explicitly conjugates the bns_operators by a Jones-Faithful transformation, the setting is silently dropped; settings.py provides JonesFaithfulTransformation.transform_symmop as the natural mechanism, making it the second suspect if get_magsymops calls it with the wrong direction/translation sign.

BNS numbering: 1-230 are the gray (type-I) groups in International-Tables order and 231-1651 the black-white groups; this explains why BNS 231 (the first black-white group, P1 1') has a trivial spatial part and why the previous probes on 231 and on the P-1 half-integer (0.5) shift could pass unpatched (0.5 is a lattice translation under inversion).

The new probes therefore use (a) a non-half-integer origin shift (0.25), which is non-trivial even for the central-rotation group P-1 (BNS 2), and (b) a basis change on a low-symmetry gray group (e.g. BNS 3 = P2) where the 2-fold axis is non-central so the rotation set must change; each failing probe verifies the transformed family differs from the standard one before asserting, so it cannot pass unpatched by accident.

Expected pre-fix failures: origin_shift_conjugation, basis_change_rotation_conjugation, orbit_covariance (the untransformed standard family is not the conjugate for a non-symmetry setting). Expected pre-fix passes (guards against over-correction): identity_setting_noop, time_label_count_invariance.

The probes test get_magsymops directly against MagneticSpaceGroup(N).symmetry_ops() as the BNS-standard reference, and are written to fail for any convention/semantics error in get_magsymops (dropped, inverted, or partially applied transformation), not just one specific defect.

I could not see the bodies of CifParser.get_magsymops or JonesFaithfulTransformation.transform_symmop in the inventory (only signatures), so the exact defective line is inferred from the import chain and the absence of any setting-handling method on MagneticSpaceGroup; the adaptive N/setting search keeps the probes valid even if the exact BNS-number-to-group mapping differs slightly from the gray/bw split assumed here.
